collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE I: SONGS, CHANTS, SPEECHES AND WELCOMES (LCA-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola sings, chants and speaks for itself: welcoming a new leader, wishing travelers luck, greeting newcomers and newborns, rallying for hard work, standing up for each other, and arguing about who gets the next verse.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Two drummers disagree about who keeps the beat at the dances: take turns, or drum together.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has kept the beat at the village dances for ten years. (friend) has just carved a new drum, twice as big and three times as loud, and wants to lead. At the last dance they both drummed at once, at different speeds, and the dancers ended up in a heap. What should the village do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The village says they will take turns, one dance each. (subject)'s dances are steady and graceful. (friend)'s are fast and wild and leave everyone gasping. The dancers decide they like both, but would like a rest between them.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The village tells them to work it out together. It takes a month of practice, with a great deal of grumbling, but at the harvest dance they play side by side, the big drum booming under the small one. It is the best music the village has ever danced to.
